subject: SLA: operational boundary & mitigation language for Order Form
messages:
From: Erin Bates <erin.bates@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Jensen <maya.jensen@acme-legal.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form + SLA redlines (ACME Renewal)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Procurement and Legal reviewed and attached a set of redlines (ACME_Redlines_v3.docx). High level asks from our side:

- Uptime: move to 99.95% for production endpoints (we'll need a clear metric definition).
- Service credits: automatic monthly credit formula capped at 50% of monthly fees; immediate application to next invoice.
- Response times: P1 = 1 hour, P2 = 4 hours, P3 = 1 business day.
- Maintenance windows: no scheduled maintenance during our business blackout (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 ET). Emergency maintenance requires 2-hour notice.

We expect Redwood to accept these or propose counter language that legal can review. Maya is looping in legal commentary. Can you confirm next steps and who on your side will own legal coordination?

Thanks —
Erin Bates
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation
Attachments: ACME_Redlines_v3.docx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Erin Bates <erin.bates@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form + SLA redlines (ACME Renewal)

Erin —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the doc. Quick reply to confirm we received them and to propose a path forward. High-level reactions:

- Uptime metric: we can discuss measurement (region-by-region vs global). For Hosted API we typically publish 99.9% across the service; 99.95% is feasible for Dedicated/reserved capacity.
- Service credits: OK to have automatic application, but we need a monthly cap and a defined credit formula (tokens/requests impacted over total). Suggest cap at 50% of monthly fees only for systemic outages (not for maintenance).
- Response times: we can align on P1/P2/P3 SLAs but need to define P1 (system-wide outage vs customer-impacting incident).
- Maintenance windows: we can agree to blackout windows for business-critical hours, and provide a notification cadence for scheduled maintenance (7 days for non-urgent; 48 hours for urgent).

Next steps I propose:
1) Irene (Legal) will take the redlines and prepare counter-language for the SLA appendix.
2) I will produce an operational compromise doc (SLA_Appendix_Proposed.pdf) that maps uptime to Dedicated vs Hosted tiers and defines the credit calc.
3) We aim to return a consolidated redline for your counsel by Tue next week (2027-08-10).

Can you confirm Acme's maximum acceptable window for scheduled maintenance per quarter so we can quantify the "no more than X hours/quarter" language?

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | jordan.blake@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Erin Bates <erin.bates@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form + SLA redlines (ACME Renewal)

Hi Erin / Jordan —

I reviewed ACME_Redlines_v3.docx and Jordan's proposed approach. Summary of recommended legal positions and edits (attached: SLA_Appendix_Legal_comments.pdf):

- Credits cap: we are willing to accept a monthly cap (suggest 50%) but need to exclude credits for customer misconfiguration and scheduled maintenance that falls within agreed windows.
- Credit calculation: prefer a time-weighted availability metric (minutes of downtime vs total minutes in billing period) with clear start/stop definitions.
- Force majeure & exceptions: add explicit language that infrastructure provider third-party outages and upstream cloud provider outages are excluded unless caused by Redwood negligence.

Operational mitigation / fallback language (new clause suggestion):
- Redwood will add an "Operational Mitigation" clause: upon detection of a degradative incident, Redwood will (a) activate a fallback model variant or reduced feature set within 2 hours for production systems when available and (b) notify ACME and provide an ETA for full remediation. This gives customers a fallback that preserves availability while remediation occurs.

Maintenance windows: we cannot guarantee zero maintenance during customer blackout hours for Hosted tier; we can offer a contractual blackout guarantee for Dedicated/reserved capacity. Proposed compromise:
- Hosted API: 99.9% uptime SLA with maintenance outside blackout hours where practicable; emergency maintenance exception with 2-hour notice.
- Dedicated: 99.95% uptime SLA, maintenance windows not to exceed 6 hours per quarter during standard off-hours unless emergency.

I will turn these edits into redline suggestions in the attached PDF. Jordan — please confirm operational feasibility on fallback timelines (2 hours) and the proposed maintenance caps so I can finalize.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA_Appendix_Legal_comments.pdf
From: Erin Bates <erin.bates@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Jensen <maya.jensen@acme-legal.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form + SLA redlines (ACME Renewal)

Jordan / Irene —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the concrete proposal. Acme's procurement and legal are generally comfortable with the compromise path you outlined with a few remaining asks:

- We accept the Hosted vs Dedicated differentiation (99.9% Hosted / 99.95% Dedicated) provided the credit calc and monthly cap are explicit.
- We need a firm commitment on response times for P1 incidents — Acme requires a 1-hour response acknowledgement for Sev1 and evidence of remediation steps within 4 hours.
- For maintenance: ACME accepts the 6 hours/quarter cap for Dedicated, but asks that you include a calendar-based blackout for our key region (US-East) during our business hours and a 2-hour heads-up for emergency maintenance.

If you can incorporate these items into a single consolidated redline (we prefer receiving a DocuSign-enabled order form once agreed), Acme will route for signature immediately upon receipt. Maya will review the final redline but doesn't expect major edits beyond tightening the P1 acknowledgement language.

Next: please share the consolidated redline and DocuSign link to procurement@acme.com. Target: finalize within this week if possible.

Best,
Erin Bates
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation
Attachments: none
